fields.name: new
fields.label: New
fields.sourceQuote: Choose New. The Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page appears.
fields.notes: Opens the Add Delegate Configuration modal (see identity ruling in page notes: treated as a modal on this page, not a separate page node). No documented role gate for who may click New.

fields.name: modify
fields.label: Modify
fields.sourceQuote: Select Modify. The Modify Delegate Configuration page appears.
fields.notes: Preceded by selecting the configuration's Name link ('Select the name of the configuration you want to modify.'), which is itself a documented navigation control equivalent to Modify (access-and-view file: 'This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page').

fields.name: remove
fields.label: Remove
fields.sourceQuote: Choose Remove, a confirmation message appears.
fields.notes: Requires a prior selection step: 'Select the configuration you want to delete in the Delegate Configurations page.' Followed by a confirmation dialog with a Yes control.

fields.name: confirm-yes
fields.label: Yes
fields.sourceQuote: Choose Yes.
fields.notes: Confirmation dialog control after Remove. The corpus never enumerates a second option for this dialog (e.g. 'No' or 'Cancel'); only 'Yes' is documented. Do not invent the other half of the pair -- record only what is attested.

fields.name: save
fields.label: Save
fields.sourceQuote: Select Save to return to the Delegate Configuration page.
fields.notes: Saves the Add/Modify Delegate Configuration modal and returns to the parent list. LABEL-DRIFT: this same Save step is described with a SINGULAR destination here ('...Delegate Configuration page') but a PLURAL destination in the edit topic ('select Save to return to the Delegate Configurations page.', edit-an-invoice-delegate-configuration-c7f51424.md) -- see the structure contradiction in contradictions[] documenting the child-surface naming drift.

fields.name: tab-selector
fields.label: Invoice / Purchase Request (tabs)
fields.sourceQuote: Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.
fields.notes: Attested FOUR independent times, one per CRUD topic, with three different verb/punctuation variants: 'Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' (access), 'On the Delegate Configurations page, select either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' (create), 'On the Delegate Configurations page, choose either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' (edit), 'On the Delegate Configurations page, Select either the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' (delete, note SAP's capital mid-sentence 'Select'). No documented control exists anywhere for the Purchase Request tab specifically -- both rosters and the child window ('Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice page') describe the Invoice side only. Do NOT mirror the Invoice roster onto Purchase Request; that tab is thin by the documentation itself.  || REPAIRED (label + fieldType), per refuter 1's named defect. The extracted label 'Invoice or Purchase Request tab' was a sentence fragment lifted from the instruction, not a UI caption - no control in the product is captioned that. Relabelled as the TAB STRIP following the built-graph precedent field.image-handling.imagingTabSelector ('Invoice Imaging / Vendor Imaging (tabs)'), and fieldType changed from 'button' to 'unknown' to match that precedent and field.company-locations.shipToTab / billToTab and field.capture-processing-admin.capture_processing_admin_tabs. The two ATTESTED tab captions 'Invoice' and 'Purchase Request' stay in validValues - both strings are printed verbatim inside the sourceQuote itself, so nothing is invented. NOT SPLIT: refuter 1 offered the Company Locations precedent of ONE FIELD PER TAB; a split would create records that never faced the adversarial refuters, so it is reported in splitsProposed and deliberately does not enter the graph. This field CROSS-REFERENCES, and must not duplicate, the page node's own tabs / tabsSourceQuote / tabsSourceFile property, which carries this same sentence. Ownership is corpus-settled: refuter 2 measured 'Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' to exactly ONE file and 'Invoice or Purchase Request tab' to exactly FOUR - all four delegate CRUD topics - so the sentence Run A briefly mis-assigned to the Workflows Approval Statuses sub-tabs is provably owned by this page.

fields.name: configuration-name
fields.label: Configuration Name
fields.sourceQuote: The name of the new delegate configuration. This is a required field.
fields.notes: Row 1 of the 6-row editor roster in the Add Delegate Configuration modal. THE ONLY DOCUMENTED REQUIRED FIELD on this page ('This is a required field.'). ALIAS COLLAPSE: the same control is column 1 of the 11-row read-only list table on the Invoice / Purchase Request tabs, where it is labelled simply 'Name' and described as 'The name of the payment delegate configuration. This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page, described in the Editing an Invoice Delegate Configuration section of this guide.' (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md) - so in the list view the value doubles as the hyperlink that opens the edit surface. No length, character-set, or uniqueness constraint is documented; no default is documented. NOT the same thing as dep.g1.059's target field name 'Delegate Configuration' - see the notes block on this extract.  || REPAIRED (value-set wiring + alias), per refuter 2's named defect. (1) MISATTACHED VALUE SET REMOVED FROM THIS FIELD'S SCOPE: the tables lens emitted a valueSetCandidate with appliesToField 'configuration_name' whose values were the TWELVE COLUMN HEADERS of the read-only list table ('Name','Can Prepare','Can Submit','Can Approve','(Any Time)','Can Approve Temporary','Can View Images','Restrict Delegates to Group','Need Approver Role to Approve','Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit','Maximum Time Period to Approve','Applies to Groups'). A column roster is not an option list for a text box, and wiring it here would resurrect seven of the aliases collapsed in this run as VALUES of an unrelated control. validValues stays [] on this field; that set must be DROPPED or re-scoped as the list-view column roster of the Invoice / Purchase Request tabs, never wired to this name. (2) ALIAS RECORDED: the list-view column label is simply 'Name', and its cell states that the value doubles as the hyperlink to the edit surface - 'This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page' (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md). (3) Name normalised from the tables lens's 'configuration_name' to the canonical 'configuration-name'; the procedure lens's identical record is folded in here (same quote, same file). CROSS-PAGE, BENIGN: label 'Configuration Name' also exists at field.image-handling.scanConfigurationName - the SCAN configuration's name, a different object on a different page. A later dedupe must not merge them.

fields.name: maximum-time-period-to-approve
fields.label: Maximum Time Period to Approve
fields.sourceQuote: Indicates a set time period, in days, for which an employee can approve invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Row 2 of the editor roster AND row 10 of the list-view roster - THE LABEL IS IDENTICAL ON BOTH SIDES (no drift here), and the description sentence is character-identical in both files, so the same quote verifies against access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md as well. UNIT IS DOCUMENTED: days. NO minimum, maximum, or default value is enumerated anywhere in the corpus - a blind build must not supply one. Both files attach the same cross-surface note; in the editor it reads 'This field works in conjunction with the Choose Dates link in the Delegates area of both My Info and User Administration.' and in the list view the same sentence is prefixed 'NOTE: '. MEASURED: 'Choose Dates' occurs exactly twice corpus-wide, both inside this page's own two rosters - which is the positive evidence that the per-delegate start/end DATES are set on My Info / User Administration and that THIS page has no date field at all.  || MERGED: the procedure-lens variant 'maximum-time-period-to-approve' cited access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md with the identical sentence. Both refuters verified the quote returns grep -F -c = 1 in EACH file, so this is a genuine double attestation, not a mis-citation. Anchored on the create (editor / modal) topic per refuter 1 so the field sits on the surface where the value is actually set. Name is the canonical hyphen spelling.

fields.name: applies-to-groups
fields.label: Applies to Groups
fields.sourceQuote: Displays the names of the groups for which the configuration applies.
fields.notes: Row 5 of the editor roster AND row 11 of the list-view roster, label and description character-identical on both sides (the same quote verifies against access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md). CARDINALITY RULE, stated twice in the editor topic with DIFFERENT PRODUCT WORDING: body prose says 'Each group within your company can only have one Invoice delegate configuration.' while this cell's Note says 'Each group within your company can only have one payment delegate configuration; however, because delegate configurations use inheritance, a configuration created for one group can be applied to all the groups below it in the hierarchy.' - 'Invoice delegate configuration' vs 'payment delegate configuration' for the same object, in one file. Recorded as an alias, not as a contradiction (one file, no substantive disagreement). THE VALUE SPACE IS THE TENANT'S GROUP HIERARCHY and is therefore correctly empty in a blind build - group names are tenant data. fieldType 'multiselect' is inferred from 'the names of the groups' (plural) and is marked as an inference. dep.g1.059 (already in the graph, targeting {page 'Delegate Configurations', field 'Delegate Configuration'}) carries this exact cardinality quote; THIS is the field it should be repointed at.  || MERGED: the procedure-lens variant 'applies-to-groups' cited access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md with the identical sentence; the quote verifies in BOTH files. Anchored on the create (editor / modal) topic. Name is the canonical hyphen spelling. fieldType 'multiselect' is an INFERENCE from 'the names of the groups' (plural) and from the built graph's convention for group-scoped fields (field.policies.editable-by-group-s, field.workflows.editable_by_groups) - the corpus never states a control type here. CROSS-PAGE, BENIGN: 'Applies to Groups' is a product-wide Concur idiom that also appears in setting-up-check-configuration-a0193517.md and understand-editable-by-groups-and-applies-to-groups-645ff499.md; those hits are NOT evidence this control lives elsewhere.

fields.name: restrictions
fields.label: Restrictions
fields.sourceQuote: The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates based on the following choices:
fields.notes: SECTION HEADING, NOT A SETTABLE CONTROL. Row 3 of the editor roster; its Description cell holds a nested TWO-ENTRY bullet catalogue that carries the actual controls (emitted separately as restrict_delegate_selection_to_users_group and require_approver_role_for_approval_delegation, and enumerated in valueSetCandidates). Emitted because it is a documented row of a settings table and because a driver needs the grouping to locate the two checkboxes. NOT a role gate: 'The Configuration administrator' here names who uses the control, not who may reach the page - there is NO documented role gate for this page anywhere in this corpus. The nested options are not enumerated with Yes/No values; the corpus describes each only as 'If active, ...', and the opposite state is NEVER enumerated, so no value list is emitted.  || REPAIRED (containment, not values), per refuter 2's named defect. The tables lens emitted a valueSetCandidate keyed appliesToField 'restrictions' whose values were this row's TWO CHILD CONTROLS ("Restrict delegate selection to user's group", 'Require approver role for approval delegation'). Both are already emitted as FIELDS on this page, so wiring that set would double-book two controls - once as fields, once as values of their own parent. That set must be RECLASSIFIED as a containment / child list or DROPPED; it must not be wired as validValues. validValues stays [] and fieldType stays 'unknown' because this row is a SECTION HEADING, not a settable control - a driver uses it only to locate the two checkboxes beneath it. Kept (not dropped) under this project's calibration rule that a row in a documented field table is a field. Re-affirmed: 'The Configuration administrator can restrict the delegates...' names who USES the control, not who may reach the page - it is NOT a role gate, and this page has no documented role gate anywhere in the corpus.

fields.name: restrict_delegate_selection_to_users_group
fields.label: Restrict delegate selection to user's group
fields.sourceQuote: Restrict delegate selection to user's group: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can only act on behalf of another employee within their group.
fields.notes: Entry 1 of 2 in the nested Restrictions catalogue. THREE-LABEL ALIAS COLLAPSE, all three grounded: editor 'Restrict delegate selection to user's group'; list-view column 'Restrict Delegates to Group' described as 'Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can select delegates that are outside of their own group.' (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md); terminology entry 'Delegate Restriction to Group: A method for designating whether an employee can select delegates outside of their own group.' (terminology-e1e1ed99.md). See the label-drift contradiction node. NOTE THE POLARITY INVERSION between the two descriptions - the editor says active means the delegate can act ONLY within group, the list-view column says it indicates whether delegates OUTSIDE the group can be selected. Both are consistent readings of one checkbox but they are phrased in opposite directions; a writer should read the checkbox state, not the prose. fieldType 'checkbox' is inferred from 'If active' plus the sibling 'check box' wording in delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md; the corpus never enumerates the on/off values, so validValues is deliberately empty.

fields.name: require_approver_role_for_approval_delegation
fields.label: Require approver role for approval delegation
fields.sourceQuote: Require approver role for approval delegation: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration must be assigned the Approver role in order to be allowed delegate approval status.
fields.notes: Entry 2 of 2 in the nested Restrictions catalogue. ALIAS: list-view column 'Need Approver Role to Approve', described as 'Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration must select delegate approvers with the approval role assigned.' (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md) - see the label-drift contradiction node. Corroborated from a third guide, which states the prerequisite as an unconditional rule rather than a setting: 'The only requirement of the delegate is that the delegate must already be an approver, that is, the delegate must already have the Invoice Approver role.' (approver-terminology-8559861c.md). That third statement is about the authorized-approver delegation path specifically and is recorded as a dependency, not as a second field. The role named is 'Approver' / 'Invoice Approver' and is set in User Permissions, not on this page. No value list is enumerated.

fields.name: restrict_approvers_to_equal_or_higher_authorized_approver_limit
fields.label: Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit
fields.sourceQuote: If selected (enabled), the user selected to be a delegate for an Authorized Approver must also be an Authorized Approver, with the same or higher approver limit.
fields.notes: Row 4 of the editor roster AND row 9 of the list-view roster, LABEL AND DESCRIPTION CHARACTER-IDENTICAL on both sides (the same quote verifies against access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md) - the one long control name that does NOT drift. TWO DOCUMENTED CONSEQUENCES, both from the editor topic's Note block: (1) 'When this setting is cleared (disabled), and a delegate with authority only for a lower approval limit is chosen, approval authority and functionality (Can Approve and Can Approve Temporary) become unavailable for that delegate' - note that the consequence sentence uses the LIST-VIEW labels for the two approve controls, inside the EDITOR topic, which is direct evidence that SAP treats the two label sets as one control set; (2) 'The Authorized Approver limits are evaluated only when the delegate is assigned.' - the limit is never re-checked, and if the approver's limit is later lowered Concur Invoice neither removes the delegate nor notifies anyone. This is the field that ties this page to the built Workflows Authorized Approvers tab and to page.authorized-approval-limits; it is a SIBLING cross-reference and must not be re-homed - the corpus never places Delegate Configurations under Workflows. Dated by the guide revision history: 'Restrict approvers to those with equal or higher authorized approver limit setting to the Add Delegate Configuration page.' (delegate-configuration-8b2bd26d.md). No value list is enumerated ('selected (enabled)' / 'cleared (disabled)' are prose states, not an option list).

fields.name: inheritance_link
fields.label: Inheritance
fields.sourceQuote: The Inheritance link works as a toggle. When selected, the link switches between Inheritance and No Inheritance.
fields.notes: A TOGGLE LINK nested inside the Applies to Groups cell of the editor roster, not a row of its own - emitted as a distinct control because it has its own documented behaviour and its own two-state caption. THIS IS THE ONLY ENUMERATED OPTION LIST ON THE ENTIRE PAGE and it is enumerated verbatim by the source sentence: the link caption switches between 'Inheritance' and 'No Inheritance'. The two values are therefore NOT a completed pair - both strings are printed in the corpus. Behaviour: 'Select the Inheritance link to apply the configuration to all groups that fall below the selected group in the hierarchy.' and 'When Inheritance is displayed, the configuration is inherited by the groups below the selected group, in the hierarchy.' The label is a link caption that mutates with state, so a driver must probe the current caption rather than assume it. NOT documented on the list-view roster at all - it exists only in the Add/Modify modal.

fields.name: delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees
fields.label: Delegate Settings For User Administrators and Employees
fields.sourceQuote: In this section, you can select any or all of the following options for both the user and the administrator:
fields.notes: SECTION HEADING, NOT A SETTABLE CONTROL. Row 6 (the last) of the editor roster; its Description cell holds the nested FIVE-ENTRY bullet catalogue that is the heart of this page (emitted separately as delegate_can_prepare / delegate_can_submit / delegate_can_approve_any_time / delegate_can_approve_during_specified_period / delegate_can_view_images, and enumerated in valueSetCandidates). 'any or all' establishes that the five are INDEPENDENT multi-select checkboxes, not a radio group. 'for both the user and the administrator' is the permission-subset model from overview-8b2ba917.md: 'The user or the User Administrator share identical sets of permissions that are available when either of them assigns a delegate, as defined in the delegate configuration.' - i.e. there is exactly ONE set of five checkboxes, not two, and the editor topic is explicit that 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' Do not model a per-role duplicate of these five.  || REPAIRED (containment, not values), per refuter 2's named defect. The tables lens emitted a valueSetCandidate keyed appliesToField 'delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees' whose values were this row's FIVE CHILD CONTROLS ('Delegate can prepare', 'Delegate can submit', 'Delegate can approve (any time)', 'Delegate can approve during specified period', 'Delegate can view images'). All five are already emitted as FIELDS on this page, so wiring that set would double-book five controls - once as fields, once as values of their own parent. RECLASSIFY as a containment / child list or DROP; do not wire it as validValues. validValues stays [] and fieldType stays 'unknown' because this row is a SECTION HEADING, not a settable control. The two structural facts are preserved above: 'any or all' establishes FIVE INDEPENDENT checkboxes rather than a radio group, and the permission-subset model plus 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' means there is exactly ONE set of five - do NOT model a per-role duplicate for the User Administrator.

fields.name: delegate_can_prepare
fields.label: Delegate can prepare
fields.sourceQuote: Delegate can prepare: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can create invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Entry 1 of 5 in the nested Delegate Settings catalogue. ALIAS: list-view column 'Can Prepare', described as 'Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can prepare invoices on behalf of another employee.' (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md). NOTE THE VERB DRIFT WITHIN THE ALIAS PAIR: the editor says 'create invoices', the list view says 'prepare invoices' - same control, two verbs. Named as a worked example of a right that is stripped on a group move: 'If the old delegate configuration had rights, such as Can Prepare, associated with it, but the new configuration does not allow prepare rights, then that delegate will no longer be able to prepare.' (special-considerations-for-payment-delegate-configurations-77a887a4.md). No on/off value list is enumerated.

fields.name: delegate_can_submit
fields.label: Delegate can submit
fields.sourceQuote: Delegate can submit: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can submit invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Entry 2 of 5 in the nested Delegate Settings catalogue. ALIAS: list-view column 'Can Submit' ('Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can submit invoices on behalf of another employee.', access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md) - the descriptions are otherwise identical apart from the label. THIS IS THE FIELD ON WHICH THE CASCADING TWO-GATE MODEL IS MADE CONCRETE: a delegate may submit 'only if that permission was granted first within the delegate configuration by the User Admin, and then when the delegate was added for the employee. This means an administrator may grant this ability, but the user can deny it when they add their delegate.' (delegates-submit-a-payment-or-purchase-request-0ee0f0b9.md) - enabling it here is necessary but NOT sufficient. Runtime consequence when denied: the delegate sees a Notify Employee link in place of Submit (when-the-delegate-cannot-submit-53c9cb69.md; that topic embeds a sample email with tenant-shaped data which is deliberately NOT quoted anywhere in this extract). No on/off value list is enumerated.

fields.name: delegate_can_approve_any_time
fields.label: Delegate can approve (any time)
fields.sourceQuote: Delegate can approve (any time): If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Entry 3 of 5 in the nested Delegate Settings catalogue; the editor sentence continues 'There is no time period associated with this action.' ALIAS: list-view column 'Can Approve' / '(Any Time)' - CAUTION, in access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md those two fragments sit on SEPARATE LINES INSIDE ONE CELL, so no verbatim quote can join them; its description is 'Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee. There is no time period associated with this action.' Becomes UNAVAILABLE for a given delegate when restrict_approvers_to_equal_or_higher_authorized_approver_limit is cleared and a lower-limit delegate is chosen. A delegate approving on behalf of an authorized approver INHERITS that approver's limits, currencies and exception authority (delegates-4d7c563c.md, corroborated by delegates-ff6ea3e6.md) - it does not use its own. Whether such a delegate may approve its OWN requests is governed off this page, by the built Workflows field 'Allow delegated approvers to approve their own requests' (delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md places it 'in the General step'); emitted here as a dependency ONLY, never as a field. No on/off value list is enumerated.

fields.name: delegate_can_approve_during_specified_period
fields.label: Delegate can approve during specified period
fields.sourceQuote: Delegate can approve during specified period: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Entry 4 of 5 in the nested Delegate Settings catalogue; the editor sentence continues 'There is a set length of time associated with this action.' THREE-LABEL ALIAS COLLAPSE: editor 'Delegate can approve during specified period'; list-view column 'Can Approve Temporary' ('Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee. There is a set time period associated with this action.', access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md); terminology entry 'Temporary Approval Delegation: A method for designating an employee to act as an approver for a specified duration of time.' (terminology-e1e1ed99.md). NOTE the third drift inside the descriptions - 'a set length of time' (editor) vs 'a set time period' (list view). PAIRED WITH maximum_time_period_to_approve, which supplies the days, and with the Choose Dates link on My Info / User Administration, which supplies the actual per-delegate dates. GOVERNANCE LEVER: this is the setting named in 'The administrator may ONLY enable temporary approval delegation, requiring employees to periodically renew their delegations to keep them in effect.' (special-considerations-for-delegate-configurations-8b2bfccb.md) - the documented mitigation for stale delegate assignments after a group move. RUNTIME SIDE EFFECT, not a control here: 'The temporary delegate (those with a specified beginning and ending date) will always automatically receive the approval invoice via email.' (delegates-email-notification-7c866769.md), whereas a permanent delegate chooses in My Info. No on/off value list is enumerated.

fields.name: delegate_can_view_images
fields.label: Delegate can view images
fields.sourceQuote: Delegate can view images: If active, the delegates assigned to this configuration can view Invoice images for invoices on behalf of another employee.
fields.notes: Entry 5 of 5 in the nested Delegate Settings catalogue. THE WORST-DRIFTING CONTROL ON THE PAGE - THREE LABELS ACROSS THREE FILES: editor 'Delegate can view images'; list-view column 'Can View Images' ('Indicates whether the employee assigned to this configuration can view the invoices received through the imaging service.', access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md); and a third, longer caption in the modal, 'To allow delegates to view invoices, select the Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests check box in the Add Delegate Configuration window.' (delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md). See the dedicated label-drift contradiction node - a driver must probe all three. The delegate-experience wording is also the only place the corpus calls any of these a 'check box' in so many words, which is what grounds fieldType checkbox for the whole Delegate Settings group. ADMIN SETTING IS OVERRIDABLE BY THE EMPLOYEE: 'Although the configuration allows a delegate to view invoice images, the employee can elect to override this setting.' - the employee clears a separate 'Can View Images check box on the Invoice Delegates page' under Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Delegates. That employee-side checkbox is an END-USER control on a different surface and is emitted as a dependency, not as a field. No on/off value list is enumerated.  || MERGED ACROSS TWO LENSES into ONE field so no duplicate name reaches the validator. The crosscut lens emitted the same control under the same name with the longer modal caption 'Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests', quoted from delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md: 'To allow delegates to view invoices, select the Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests check box in the Add Delegate Configuration window.' (verified verbatim by both refuters). That file is also the ONLY place the corpus says 'check box' outright for this group, which is what grounds fieldType checkbox for all five Delegate Settings controls, and it supplies the only full modal path: 'This window is available by clicking Administration > Invoice > Delegate Configurations > New (or Modify, if existing configuration).' THREE ADMIN LABELS a driver must be able to probe: 'Delegate can view images' (editor), 'Can View Images' (list column), 'Delegate can view invoice images for payment requests' (delegate-experience). ADMIN / END-USER LABEL COLLISION, measured by refuter 2: the identical string 'Can View Images' ALSO names the EMPLOYEE-side checkbox on a different surface - 'the Can View Images check box on the Invoice Delegates page by clicking Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Delegates' - which can OVERRIDE this admin setting. That end-user control stays a DEPENDENCY into the unbuilt Profile / Invoice Settings surface and must never become a field here. Also from that file: 'The Invoice Admin sets this option when defining delegates.' names the MENU alias, not a role - it is NOT a role gate.

fields.label: Can Approve (Any Time)
fields.sourceQuote: Indicates whether the employees assigned to this configuration can approve invoices on behalf of another employee. There is no time period associated with this action.

verifyNotes:
GROUNDING, RE-RUN MECHANICALLY BY ME, NOT INHERITED: all 20 emitted sourceQuotes verify with grep -F -c >= 1 against their cited file (every one returned exactly 1). All 20 sourceFiles exist and use the required '<guide-dir>/<filename>.md' form; none carries the forbidden CONCUR_INVOICE/ prefix. All 20 cite admin-guides, which is correct - refuter 1 measured ZERO tools-guides files bearing a Delegate Configuration control. I additionally grep-verified every quote I HAND-TYPED into repaired notes: 'This is also a link to the Edit Delegate Configuration page' (1), 'Select the Invoice or Purchase Request tab.' (1), the delegate-experience view-images caption (1), the full modal path 'This window is available by clicking Administration > Invoice > Delegate Configurations > New (or Modify, if existing configuration).' (1), 'the Can View Images check box on the Invoice Delegates page by clicking Profile > Profile Settings > Invoice Delegates' (1), 'The Invoice Admin sets this option when defining delegates.' (1), and 'There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles.' (1). I also confirmed the two MERGED fields are genuinely double-attested rather than mis-cited: the Maximum Time Period and Applies to Groups sentences each return 1 hit in BOTH create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md and access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md. fromRawHtmlTable is false on all 20, which matches the measured census (grep -c '<table' = 0 across every file in this page's candidate set).

WHAT THE REFUTERS FOUND AT PAGE LEVEL, AND WHAT I DID.
(1) ALIAS COLLAPSE - both refuters independently mapped seven label-drift pairs plus two exact duplicates and dropped nine records. I carried every one of those nine into 'dropped' with duplicateOf, and confirmed by reading each survivor's notes that the dropped label, its description and its sourceFile survive as text on the survivor. Post-collapse: 12 settable data controls + 2 section headings + 6 procedure controls = 20 records, i.e. exactly the 11-13 unique-control band the map predicted and well clear of the discredited ~25 recon estimate. NOTHING WAS PADDED TO HIT A NUMBER.
(2) THREE MISATTACHED VALUE SETS - the biggest non-quote defect on this page and invisible to bin/validate-graph.py. I could not fix them in this artefact (the roster shape carries no valueSets), so I did the next best thing: I made the repair explicit in each affected field's notes and I state it here for the merger. DROP OR RE-SCOPE, DO NOT WIRE: appliesToField 'configuration_name' whose 12 'values' are the LIST-VIEW COLUMN HEADERS (wiring it would resurrect seven aliases collapsed in this run as VALUES of an unrelated text box - and the name no longer exists anyway, it is now 'configuration-name'); appliesToField 'restrictions' (its 2 'values' are child CONTROLS already emitted as fields); appliesToField 'delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees' (its 5 'values' are child CONTROLS already emitted as fields). Those last two must be reclassified as containment / child lists or dropped - as written they double-book seven controls on one page, once as fields and once as values. EXACTLY ONE GENUINE VALUE SET SURVIVES ON THIS PAGE: appliesToField 'inheritance_link' = ['Inheritance','No Inheritance'], both strings printed verbatim in the one source sentence. I deliberately kept the survivor named 'inheritance_link' (not 'inheritance-toggle') so that set stays wired - the rule-7 failure mode that stranded 17 sets in an earlier run.
(3) INVENTED-VALUE SWEEP - clean, and I re-checked it. Only two of the 20 records carry any validValues, and in both cases every string is printed inside that record's own sourceQuote: tab-selector ['Invoice','Purchase Request'] and inheritance_link ['Inheritance','No Inheritance']. All seven permission checkboxes carry [] - CORRECT, because the corpus says only 'If active, ...' and 'If selected (enabled)' and NEVER enumerates the opposite state. No No/Yes pair was completed anywhere. Likewise the delete dialog documents only 'Yes' and no counterpart was invented.
(4) DEPENDENCY REWIRING IS MANDATORY AFTER THIS COLLAPSE OR EDGES DANGLE. Repoint every dependencyCandidate sourceField as follows: can-approve-any-time / can_approve_any_time -> delegate_can_approve_any_time (3 edges); can-approve-temporary / can_approve_temporary -> delegate_can_approve_during_specified_period (2); can-submit -> delegate_can_submit (1); need-approver-role-to-approve -> require_approver_role_for_approval_delegation (1); restrict-approvers-equal-or-higher-limit -> restrict_approvers_to_equal_or_higher_authorized_approver_limit (3); applies_to_groups -> applies-to-groups; maximum_time_period_to_approve -> maximum-time-period-to-approve; configuration_name -> configuration-name; inheritance-toggle -> inheritance_link. One crosscut dependencyCandidate carries an EMPTY sourceField ('') and needs a target assigned by hand. Refuter 2 checked the far ends against the built graph: authorized_approver_checkbox and approval_limit_amount (page.authorized-approval-limits), authorized_approver_level, authorized_approver_list_approver and allow_delegated_approvers_to_approve_own_requests (page.workflows) and 'Is Inheritable' (page.group-configurations) all exist by exactly those names and will resolve. The User Administration / My Info / Profile > Invoice Settings endpoints and the external 'Shared: Delegate Configuration Setup Guide' are legitimately unresolved - an unbuilt surface and one DOCUMENTARY gap.
(5) NAMING CONVENTION - the surviving set deliberately mixes hyphen names from the procedure lens (tab-selector, configuration-name, maximum-time-period-to-approve, applies-to-groups, new, modify, remove, confirm-yes, save) with underscore names from the tables lens (delegate_can_*, restrict_*, require_*, inheritance_link, restrictions, delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees). Refuter 2 flagged this as the one assembler decision left. I did NOT normalise, because my hard constraint forbids emitting any name that is not on the KEEP or REPAIR list, and normalising would invent nine names nobody adjudicated. The built graph is itself split on this (page.policies uses UI labels, page.workflows uses snake_case), so this is a cosmetic pass for the merger, not a defect.

THE FOUR REPAIRS I ACTUALLY MADE. (a) tab-selector: label 'Invoice or Purchase Request tab' -> 'Invoice / Purchase Request (tabs)' (a sentence fragment is not a UI caption; relabelled as the tab strip per field.image-handling.imagingTabSelector), and fieldType 'button' -> 'unknown' to match that precedent. Quote and validValues untouched and re-verified. (b) configuration-name: the misattached 12-value column-header set is repudiated in notes, validValues stays [], and the list-view alias 'Name' plus its hyperlink behaviour are recorded. (c) restrictions and (d) delegate_settings_for_user_administrators_and_employees: their child-control value sets are reclassified in notes as containment lists, validValues stays [] on both, and fieldType stays 'unknown' because both rows are SECTION HEADINGS, not settable controls - kept under this project's rule that a row in a documented field table is a field, and because a driver needs the grouping to find the two and five checkboxes beneath them.

NO SPLITS EMITTED. One split is genuinely supported by the documentation (tab-selector into a per-tab pair) and is reported in splitsProposed only. Records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuters, and mis-assignment to the wrong page is precisely what grep cannot catch - so 20 inputs produced 20 records, never more.

IDENTITY, CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED: the Add / Modify / Edit Delegate Configuration child surface is a MODAL ON THIS PAGE, not a separate page node - no menu destination of its own, no role gate of its own, and decisively no object model of its own (it edits the same single configuration object the parent lists, and the corpus documents the SAME controls twice, once as the modal's entry form and once as the parent's read-only columns). That is the Workflows General/Steps/Step Rules wizard pattern, not the Authorized Approval Limits pattern. Consequently the modal's fields (everything except tab-selector, New, Modify, Remove and Yes) are emitted here and are DISPLAYED read-only as list columns on the Invoice and Purchase Request tabs. The EIGHT-name label drift for that one surface is a grounded contradiction in its own right and belongs on the page node.

dep.g1.059 WILL NOT AUTO-RESOLVE AND I DID NOT CONTORT NAMING TO FORCE IT. Its targetRef is {page:'Delegate Configurations', field:'Delegate Configuration', resolved:false} - a LABEL-shaped target. This run emits 'configuration-name' (label 'Configuration Name') and no field literally called 'Delegate Configuration'. Reported for a correction pass: the honest fix is repointing it at 'applies-to-groups', whose own cell repeats its cardinality rule. Its independent corroboration of the PAGE NAME stands either way.

BOUNDARIES HELD. Not one emitted field is sourced from delegate-self-approval-1b627285.md - I verified that across all 20 records; it is cited only in notes and dependencies, which is the permitted use, and the built field.workflows.allow-delegated-approvers-to-approve-own-requests (sourced from create-a-new-workflow-554e86aa.md) is untouched. No field is taken from the two consumer surfaces (invoice-user-f11cccd8.md, user-administrator-5aa3eb5e.md) or from when-the-delegate-cannot-submit-53c9cb69.md, whose sample tenant-shaped email block is quoted NOWHERE. The database table name CT_AUTHORIZED_APPROVER appears nowhere. The '2 user interfaces' 2014 boilerplate was NOT turned into a uiVariant claim - uiVariant is 'undifferentiated' on the page and on all 20 fields.

THIN FINDINGS THAT ARE THE CORRECT ANSWER, NOT GAPS I FAILED TO FILL. (i) NO Purchase Request field roster exists anywhere in this corpus. The tab is named four independent times and not one control is attributed to it; both rosters and the modal title ('Add Delegate Configuration - Invoice') describe the Invoice side. A driver has no roster for that tab, and mirroring the Invoice roster onto it would be fabrication. (ii) NO start-date / end-date / expiration field exists on this page - 'Choose Dates' occurs exactly twice corpus-wide, both times inside this page's own rosters, both times pointing OUT to My Info and User Administration. (iii) NO documented role gate for this page anywhere in the corpus; roleGates:[] is a measured absence, and the two role-shaped sentences name who USES a field and the MENU alias respectively. (iv) Almost no enumerated value lists: one only. (v) Two genuine contradictions are recorded rather than reconciled - the restrict-delegates-to-group POLARITY inversion, and the group-move tension between special-considerations-for-delegate-configurations-8b2bfccb.md ('the system will not remove or update existing delegate assignments') and special-considerations-for-payment-delegate-configurations-77a887a4.md (rights 'removed automatically'); the corpus does not say whether they scope assignment existence or individual rights, so neither is picked.

MUST-READ FILES: the two refuters between them opened every must-read. For my repair lens I re-read the two rosters (access-and-view-payment-delegate-configurations-8ed1298f.md, create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md) and delegate-experience-8b30fb06.md (CORRECTED 2026-09-01: that file is cited by a contradiction and a dependency, NOT by any emitted field) (edit-...-c7f51424.md, delete-...-92627a9b.md), which I also verified quotes against. I did not re-open the ten notes-only must-reads (overview-8b2ba917, terminology-e1e1ed99, both special-considerations, delegates-4d7c563c, delegates-ff6ea3e6, delegates-submit-...-0ee0f0b9, audit-invoice-delegate-actions-3660a51f, invoice-user-f11cccd8, user-administrator-5aa3eb5e): no emitted record cites any of them as a sourceFile, both refuters read or spot-verified them, and refuter 1 independently confirmed each load-bearing secondary sentence at 1 hit. That is an honest skip, stated rather than silent.

COVERAGE JUDGEMENT - 'partial', and I mean it literally. Real field-level documentation exists, but it is confined to TWO topics describing ONE object from two sides; a whole tab has no roster; there is no role gate; and enumerated value lists are almost entirely absent. | POST-CRITIC 2026-09-01: SEVEN list-view column fields RESTORED (can-approve-any-time, can-approve-temporary, can-prepare, can-submit, can-view-images, need-approver-role-to-approve, restrict-delegates-to-group) - both critics independently reversed that alias-collapse drop, and the built Workflows page decides the identical two-file shape the same way. THE PAGE SEMANTICS, which had no merge-bound carrier: "Concur Invoice delegate configurations define the subset of invoice permissions that delegates are allowed to have within Concur Invoice." (overview-8b2ba917.md) and "The configuration is a template that allows or denies permissions to the user or the User Admin. The subset of permissions is identical. There is no option to provide separate permissions for specific employees or by their assigned roles." (create-a-new-invoice-delegate-configuration-fcf42662.md). THE SIX-ENTRY DELEGATE TERMINOLOGY CATALOGUE from terminology-e1e1ed99.md reached the merge at 3 of 6; the three lost are Invoice Request Delegates, Purchase Request Delegates and Delegated Approver. The corpus enumerates THREE delegate kinds against a TWO-tab page and never maps them - UNDETERMINED BY THE DOCUMENTATION, recorded here rather than resolved. dep.g1.059 cannot resolve as written (its field name "Delegate Configuration" is label-shaped); the repoint target is applies-to-groups.
